domain_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up the payment/checkout step for purchasing a domain. Use {{vendor}} (my configured payments vendor) to create a checkout for the domain quote — do not name or assume any other payments provider.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: the domain name I want to buy, the quoted price/currency for it (from the registrar), and confirmation that I have {{vendor}} credentials configured in this environment.

Then, using {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard tooling with my configured credentials:
1. Create a product/price (or transaction/order, per {{vendor}}'s model) representing this domain quote.
2. Generate a checkout session or payment link for that price — either a hosted checkout page or a shareable payment link, whichever {{vendor}} supports.
3. If {{vendor}} offers a sandbox/test mode, first provision a sandbox and run the checkout flow there to confirm it works end-to-end before touching live mode.
4. Prepare a clear summary for me: the domain name, price, currency, the checkout/payment link URL, and whether it's sandbox or live.

Do NOT capture payment, complete the order, or move money — payment approval is a spend gate that requires my explicit sign-off. Once everything is drafted and the checkout link is ready, present it to me along with the summary and stop for human sign-off. I will personally review and approve/pay before any charge is finalized.

Report back with: the checkout/payment link, the product/price or transaction ID created, confirmation of sandbox vs. live mode, and a short checklist of what I need to verify before approving payment.

domain_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me complete step domain_002:n2 — Register a domain at Name.com as part of my end-to-end domain purchase flow (payment already handled via Stripe; DNS/SSL will be connected via Cloudflare in a later step).

Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have:
- The exact domain name (including TLD) I want to register
- The registrant contact details (name, address, email, phone) to use for the registration, or confirmation to use the details already on file in my Name.com account
- Confirmation of desired registration length (e.g., 1 year) and whether I want privacy protection and auto-renew enabled

Once you have these, use my configured credentials to access Name.com and initiate the domain registration via the dashboard or API, entering the registrant details, registration period, and privacy/auto-renew preferences I provided. Since this is an async operation, the registration may not complete instantly — after submitting, poll or check the domain's status in my Name.com account until it shows as fully registered and active (not pending or failed). If the registration fails or requires additional verification (such as ICANN email confirmation), report exactly what is needed from me.

Done looks like: the domain appears in my Name.com account as registered and active, with correct registrant details, chosen registration length, and privacy/auto-renew settings applied as requested.

Report back to me with: the domain name, registration status (active/pending/failed), expiration date, whether privacy protection and auto-renew are enabled, and any follow-up action required from me (e.g., confirming an ICANN verification email). Do not proceed to DNS/SSL setup — that is a separate step.

domain_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me provision DNS and SSL for a newly purchased domain using {{vendor}}, as part of an automated domain-setup workflow. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the domain name just purchased, (2) the destination for the domain — e.g. the IP address, hostname, or deployed service it should point to, and (3) whether I want a wildcard subdomain covered.

Using your configured credentials, invoke {{vendor}}'s API endpoints (DNS record creation, SSL settings) via the Code Mode MCP execute tool to: 1) add the domain to {{vendor}} if it isn't already active there, 2) create the necessary DNS records (A/CNAME as appropriate) pointing to the destination I gave you, including a wildcard record if requested, 3) enable automatic, auto-renewing TLS/SSL for the domain (and wildcard if applicable), and 4) attach the custom domain to the target deployed service if one was specified.

Because DNS propagation and certificate issuance happen asynchronously, after submitting the changes you must poll {{vendor}}'s status for the domain/zone and the SSL certificate until DNS is active and the certificate shows as issued/active, or until a reasonable timeout (e.g. 15-20 minutes) is reached — report back if it times out so I can check manually.

When done, report back: the domain name, the DNS records created, the SSL/TLS mode enabled, whether wildcard coverage is active, the final verified status (active/issued) or the timeout/error encountered, and any {{vendor}} dashboard link useful for me to review the configuration.
